recognize_zh: 骨髓抹片幾乎全被大小不一的母細胞取代，核質比高、染色質細緻、核形不規則或有凹陷，細胞質少且淡藍無顆粒，部分呈拖尾的手鏡狀（hand-mirror）；單一形態母細胞成片且無顆粒，符合急性淋巴母細胞白血病復發。
features: Marrow replaced by a monotonous population of blasts with only rare residual normal cells
Variable blast size (small to large) with high N:C ratio
Round to irregular, indented or cleaved nuclei with finely dispersed chromatin; occasional small nucleoli
Scant pale to moderately basophilic agranular cytoplasm, some with hand-mirror tails and small vacuoles
Smudged cells and platelet clumps in background; no Auer rods
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear is diffusely replaced by blasts that vary from small to large, with high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratios, round to irregular or indented nuclei, finely dispersed chromatin and occasional small nucleoli. The cytoplasm is scant, agranular and pale blue, with some cells showing hand-mirror projections; Auer rods are not seen. Normal hematopoietic elements are markedly reduced. In a child with previously treated precursor B-ALL, findings are consistent with relapsed acute lymphoblastic leukemia, to be confirmed by flow cytometry and cytogenetic/molecular studies.

ddx.vs: Myeloblasts often show fine azurophilic granules or Auer rods and are MPO positive, whereas lymphoblasts are agranular and MPO negative.
Hematogones have more condensed homogeneous chromatin, rarely efface the marrow, and show normal maturation without aberrant antigens on flow cytometry.
Burkitt cells have deeply basophilic cytoplasm with prominent lipid vacuoles and a mature B-cell (surface immunoglobulin-positive, TdT-negative) phenotype.

ddx.dx: Metastatic small round blue cell tumor (neuroblastoma, rhabdomyosarcoma)
ddx.vs: Small round cell tumors form cohesive clusters or rosettes and are CD45 negative, unlike discohesive lymphoblasts.
